subject: Segmented GPU commitment proposal for regulated deployment - Nova Health
messages:
From: Hannah Cole <h.cole@novahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@novahealth.com>, Nova Health Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Segmented commitment ask — sizing info attached

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send an initial demand profile for the pilot and expected production ramp so your team can recommend whether Nova should take Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or pursue a Private deployment for our regulated imaging workflows. The attached spreadsheet has expected requests per day and average sequence length for Q3–Q4.

Quick context: pilot (Q3) will be limited to two hospitals (burst pattern during business hours, ~1k calls/day peak), production (Q4) expands to 12 hospitals (steady 24/7, ~18k calls/day). Latency SLO: 150–300 ms p50 for single-model path; region: US-EAST preferred. Data residency and audit trail requirements mean we cannot tolerate multitenant co-mingling in the same GPU pools.

Can your team outline a recommendation and a rough committed GPU profile with price delta and lead time for each option? We need something procurement can review by the end of next week.

Attachments: nova_demand_profile_q3_q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Hannah Cole
Senior Procurement Manager
Nova Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmented commitment ask — sizing info attached

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the detailed profile, attaching our sizing assumptions and a quick model. Marcus (serving runtime lead) and Laura (solutions) are looped in. We'll run a short modelling pass and get you a side-by-side: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, SLA) vs Private (VPC or on-prem with customer-managed network and audit controls).

Preliminary clarifying Qs that will change the sizing:
- Are the 18k calls/day evenly distributed or is there a 20% daily peak window?
- Pilot expected concurrency during business hours (Q3) — is 120 concurrent sessions a safe upper bound?
- Do you require HW-backed KMS/HSM in the Private option?

I'll schedule a 30-minute call this Thursday so we can confirm assumptions. If procurement needs a price / lead-time table, we can include optional burst capacity and a canary rollback plan.

Attachments: redwood_sizing_assumptions_v1.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Regulated Industries
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: segmented commitment ask — initial modeling notes

Irene / Laura —

Drafted a quick modelling CSV (dedicated_vs_private_modeling.csv) with three scenarios based on the demand profile Hannah sent:
1) Pilot-only reserved pool: 4 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (steady business hours peaks) — cost estimate = reserved monthly commit + burst pool for evening spikes.
2) Production reserved pool (12 hospitals): 20 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs scaled to 95% utilization with autoscale buffer — lowest per-token cost, predictable SLA, ~6–8 week procurement lead.
3) Private (VPC-dedicated nodes or on-prem): 14 x A100-80GB equiv for base (lower overcommit to satisfy isolation + audit), plus 20% buffer for failure domains — higher ops overhead, longer lead if on-prem hardware procurement required, extra cost for HSM/KMS integration.

Key tradeoffs:
- Dedicated reduces per-token cost at higher utilization; Private gives control over networking and key material but requires extra headroom for isolation and reserves.
- For regulated imaging, we should size Private with higher headroom (15–25%) to avoid noisy-neighbor risk when customer manages networking but still needs consistent latency.

I'll drop the CSV in the thread and include a short column with lead times, procurement prerequisites (PO, SOC2 evidence), and recommended canary plan (1-week staggered rollout).

Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Cole <h.cole@novahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@novahealth.com>, Nova Health Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmented commitment ask — sizing info attached

Thanks — quick answers to your clarifying Qs:
- 18k calls/day target is surface average; expect two 2-hour windows that push 30% above average (approx 3.6k calls during those windows).
- Pilot concurrency: 140 concurrent sessions during business hours.
- Yes, we require HW-backed KMS and dedicated audit retention for logs (7 years). On-prem procurement is an option for some sites but we prefer a VPC-hosted Private deployment if the security controls meet our posture.

If you can show the cost delta with the buffer numbers Marcus suggested and a proposed procurement checklist (SOC2 artifacts, IP whitepaper, contact for FedRAMP guidance), procurement will take it to legal. We are on a tight review cycle — need a decision recommendation and price comparison by EOW (next Friday).

Hannah
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <h.cole@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Nova Health Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmented commitment ask — sizing info attached

Hannah / team —

Action summary and recommendation (short):
- Recommendation: For Nova Health's ramp profile we recommend a hybrid path: Reserved Dedicated for Q3 pilot (short-term reserved commit to guarantee capacity and fast time-to-value) + a staged Private conversion for high-security sites in Q4. This minimizes per-token cost during peak production while providing the isolation and KMS/HSM controls for regulated sites.
- Sizing (high-level): Pilot (Q3): 5 x A100-80GB equiv (reserved) with 20% burst headroom. Production (Q4 baseline): 22 x A100-80GB equiv (reserved) for the main fleet + up to 6 x A100-80GB equiv provisioned as Private nodes assigned to regulated sites (sized with 25% headroom). Detailed CSV attached.
- Estimated delta: Private path (VPC + HSM) approx +28–35% total TCO vs reserved Dedicated at 90% utilization (includes HSM, extra logging retention costs). Lead times: reserved seats — 2–6 weeks; Private with client-managed network + HSM — 6–12 weeks depending on procurement.
- Procurement checklist to attach: SOC2 Type II report, network diagram template, KMS integration guidance, DocuSign purchase schedule.

Next steps:
1) We'll post the detailed modelling CSV and a short one-page procurement checklist by EOD today.
2) If procurement signs the EULA and issues a PO for the pilot reserved pool, we can lock lead times and push an SOW.
3) We'll include an optional canary plan to move two sites to Private nodes in Q4 and measure latency and audit outcomes.

Attachments: dedicated_vs_private_modeling.csv (CSV), redwood_sizing_assumptions_v1.pdf (PDF)

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/E-123456789
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8742

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to review the numbers live.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Regulated Industries
Redwood Inference
